newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's July trade deficit drops 26 pct vs June.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's July trade deficit drops 26 pct vs June.

text.p: Jordan's trade deficit fell 26 percent in July to 133.6 million dinars ($189 million) from the previous month, helped by lower imports, the Central Bank latest statistical bulletin received by Reuters showed.
But the July deficit was still 22-percent higher from 109.2 million dinars in the same month last year.
Economists said growth in non-traditional exports and a pickup in world prices of Jordan's key currency earners, posphate and potash, have helped improve exports.

Exports to traditional neighbouring markets captured the key share, with a 103 million dinars of goods sold to Arab markets compared to 98 million dinars in June. Some improvement in non-traditional outlets such as Malaysia, Australia, Turkey Korea and New Zealand helped diversify the pattern of exports.
